personas.title: Health worker (HW)
personas.description: Health workers facilitate education sessions, administer immunizations, provide counselling when needed, record vaccinations administered, record stock movements and compile, generate, and submit reports.

personas.title: Community health worker
personas.description: Community health workers provide health education, referral and follow-up, case management and basic preventive health care and home visiting services to specific communities. They provide support and assistance to clients by reminding them to get their vaccinations, responding to emergencies and reporting births.

personas.title: EPI Manager
personas.description: Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) managers develop annual and multi-annual plans, immunization communication and mobilization, management of cold chain and vaccine logistics, monitoring, supervision and evaluation of immunization services, and coordination of EPI activities at the national and subnational levels.

personas.title: Caregiver
personas.description: Mother, father, guardian, carer of the child, infant, elderly or disabled person.

personas.title: Client
personas.description: In the context of this document, a client is a person who intends to receive immunization services from the targeted health worker personas. A client who is 15 years of age or younger is considered a child.

personas.title: Child
personas.description: A client who is 15 years of age or younger and who intends to receive immunization services from the targeted health worker personas.

personas.title: System administrator
personas.description: A systems administrator, or a dedicated electronic immunization registry (EIR) staff, supervises the operation and storage of electronic health records and makes sure the server functions properly to allow clients and staff to communicate with each other, coordinate their actions and take care of essential tasks.

personas.title: Clerical staff
personas.description: A clerical staff assists in scheduling appointments, answers phone calls, greets clients, keeps/documents medical records and handles medical billing.

processes.title: Vaccination location registration
processes.objectives: All vaccination locations (including private sector facilities, government centres and/or other entities involved in public health efforts) able to administer vaccines must be registered and uniquely identified to enable appropriate tracking of vaccine coverage and stock. In the case of a health-care facility with multiple vaccination locations, only the facility will be registered.

processes.title: Plan service delivery
processes.objectives: In preparation for a vaccination session, ensure sufficient supply and organize workload

processes.title: Client registration
processes.objectives: Create and/or update the clients’ vaccine record by including personal data in the EIR to support future vaccine administration

processes.title: Administer vaccine
processes.objectives: To determine which vaccines a client needs, administer those and record the relevant necessary data both in the EIR as well as in the appropriate paper records

processes.title: Client reminder
processes.objectives: To remind clients it is time to return for a vaccine

processes.title: Defaulter tracing
processes.objectives: To identify those who are overdue for a vaccine and reach out to them to schedule their vaccination

processes.title: Resolve duplicate client records
processes.objectives: To identify duplicate client records and consolidate them into one most accurate/suitable record

processes.title: Resolve duplicate vaccination events
processes.objectives: To identify duplicate vaccination events within a client record and update into one event

processes.title: Report generation
processes.objectives: To provide the ability to access and analyse data and to improve immunization programme decision-making
